qa_pairs.expected_answer: Students are expected to attend at least 80% of scheduled sessions in courses that record attendance. A syllabus may set a higher threshold when required by accreditation, laboratory safety, or clinical practice, but it may not set a lower threshold.

qa_pairs.question: What academic requirements must an undergraduate complete to be eligible to graduate?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An undergraduate must complete at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00. contexts.text: An undergraduate student is academically eligible to graduate after completing at least 120 applicable credits, all programme-required courses, the capstone requirement, and a cumulative GPA of at least 2.00.
At least 30 of the final 45 applicable credits must be completed at Northstar University unless an approved exchange agreement states otherwise.

qa_pairs.question: What does the Northstar Merit Scholarship cover, and what does it not cover?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition but does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees.

contexts.text: The Northstar Merit Scholarship covers 50% of undergraduate tuition but does not cover student-services fees, late fees, or late-add fees.

qa_pairs.question: I missed the standard add/drop period for Fall 2026. What approvals and payment does a late add require, and what happens if I pay the fee late?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A late add is possible from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. It requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add, and the fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

contexts.text: Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date. A late add requires instructor approval, programme-director approval, and payment of a USD 40 late-add fee per course within two business days of approval. Failure to pay on time cancels the late add.

The late-add fee is USD 40 per course and must be paid within two business days after the approvals described in `02_course_registration.md`. The late-add fee is non-refundable unless the university cancels the course or confirms an administrative error.

qa_pairs.question: If I drop a single Fall 2026 course after standard add/drop but before the census date, how much tuition is reversed, and are the mandatory term fees refunded?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, which is September 4 for Fall 2026, 50% of that course's tuition is reversed. Mandatory term fees are refundable only when the student withdraws from every course before classes begin.

contexts.text: For a course dropped by the end of standard add/drop, 100% of that course's tuition is reversed. From the day after standard add/drop through the census date, 50% is reversed. After census, no tuition is reversed for an ordinary course withdrawal. Mandatory term fees are refundable only when the student withdraws from every course before classes begin.
The census date is September 4.

qa_pairs.question: I hold the Merit Scholarship and want to drop from 12 to 9 graded credits before the census date. What happens to my scholarship?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Dropping below 12 graded credits on or before the census date triggers an immediate eligibility review, because renewal requires at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term together with a term GPA of at least 3.30 and a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20. The census date governs scholarship credit-load review, and dropping on or before it may change billed credits and scholarship status.

contexts.text: Dropping below 12 graded credits on or before the census date triggers an immediate eligibility review.

To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.

The census date is important for enrolment status, tuition adjustment, and scholarship credit-load review. Dropping a course before or on the census date may change the student's billed credits and scholarship status.

qa_pairs.question: My final grade contains an arithmetic error. What are the steps and deadlines to appeal it, and who reviews the appeal first?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: First request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must then be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify a permitted ground such as calculation error. The department chair reviews a grade appeal first.

contexts.text: A disagreement about academic judgement is handled first with the instructor. Alleged calculation error, procedural unfairness, discrimination, or inconsistency with the published syllabus may proceed to the formal grade-appeal route in `08_student_support_and_appeals.md`.

The student must first request clarification from the instructor within five business days after the final grade is published. A formal grade appeal must be filed within ten business days after publication and must identify at least one permitted ground: calculation error, material departure from the published syllabus, procedural unfairness, or prohibited discrimination.
The department chair reviews a grade appeal first.

qa_pairs.question: I simply stopped attending a Fall 2026 course in November without using the portal. Does that count as a withdrawal, and what grade should I expect?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal. The student remains enrolled and may receive a failing grade. The last day to withdraw from a Fall 2026 course with a `W` grade was October 30, so after that deadline a withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition.

contexts.text: After census and through the withdrawal deadline in `01_academic_calendar.md`, the course receives a `W`. After that deadline, withdrawal requires an exceptional-circumstances petition. Stopping attendance is not a withdrawal.
A student who stops attending without dropping or withdrawing remains enrolled and may receive a failing grade.
The last day to withdraw from a course with a `W` grade is October 30

qa_pairs.question: I have finished every course and the capstone but still owe tuition. Can my degree be conferred and can I get my final transcript?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: No. An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold that blocks official transcripts and graduation clearance. Degree conferral requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds; the financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements but blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until it is resolved.

contexts.text: Degree conferral also requires clearance of financial, library, conduct, and document holds. A financial hold does not erase completed academic requirements, but it blocks official conferral and release of the final transcript until resolved under `03_tuition_payment_refund.md`.
An unpaid balance after the grace period receives a USD 75 late-payment fee and a financial hold. The hold blocks new registration, official transcripts, and graduation clearance.

qa_pairs.question: My father pays my tuition and asked the university for my grades and for a correction of my recorded personal data. What does the policy allow, and where should each request go?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information; the university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization. Requests to correct inaccurate personal data go to the Records Office, while requests to change an academic decision must use the relevant appeal process. Cases should be submitted through the portal with the case number kept, and sensitive evidence must not be sent through public chat.

contexts.text: The university may discuss a student's record only with the student or a person who has a valid, recorded authorization. A parent or sponsor who pays tuition does not automatically receive academic or conduct information. Students may download their own enrolment and billing records from the portal. Requests to correct inaccurate personal data go to the Records Office; requests to change an academic decision must use the relevant appeal process.
Students should submit cases through the portal and keep the case number. Sensitive evidence must not be sent through public chat or included in a general support ticket.

qa_pairs.question: I first discussed a late add with my instructor in late July 2026 but submitted the request on August 20, 2026. Which registration policy version applies, what does the late add cost, and how late may it be added?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: Version 2.0 applies. The policy in force on the triggering event date controls, and for registration that date is the registration action date, which is August 20, 2026, not the July discussion. Under version 2.0 a late add is allowed only through the census date and costs USD 40 per course, instead of the version 1.0 window of seven calendar days after standard add/drop at USD 25.

contexts.text: Registration Policy version 1.0, effective before August 1, 2026, allowed late adds for seven calendar days after standard add/drop and charged USD 25. Version 2.0, effective August 1, 2026, allows late adds only through census and charges USD 40 per course. A late-add request made on or after August 1, 2026 follows version 2.0 even if the student first discussed the request in July.

The policy in force on the triggering event date controls unless a newer policy explicitly states that it applies retroactively. A newer publication does not silently rewrite an earlier transaction. When the event spans multiple dates, use the date identified by the policy: for registration it is the registration action date, for tuition refunds it is the recorded drop or withdrawal date, and for scholarship review it is the end of the reviewed term.
Version 2.0 introduces a late-add window from the end of standard add/drop through the census date.

qa_pairs.question: I hold the Merit Scholarship and must pause my studies. How does an approved medical leave differ from a voluntary leave for employment for keeping the award, and does either consume my one term of probation?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity, which is the single term of probation normally granted after a first failed academic renewal requirement. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award: the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date. Either way the leave request itself must be submitted before the census date with the reason, any required documentation, and programme approval.

contexts.text: An approved medical leave pauses the scholarship for up to two consecutive regular terms and does not consume the one-term probation opportunity. A voluntary leave for employment or travel does not automatically reserve the award; the student must request a scholarship deferral before the census date.
A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss.

A standard leave may last one or two consecutive regular terms. The student must submit the request before the census date, explain the reason, provide any required documentation, and obtain programme approval.

qa_pairs.question: A documented illness forced me to withdraw from all my courses after the census date. Will I receive money back, how is the amount calculated, and how does my scholarship affect it?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and it requires the medical process in the leave and withdrawal policy. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated, so a refund estimate shown before scholarship adjustment is not final. A retroactive medical request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation.

contexts.text: An approved medical withdrawal may receive a pro-rated tuition credit for future study, calculated from the last documented date of participation. It is not a cash refund and requires the process in `06_leave_and_withdrawal.md`. Scholarship funds are adjusted before any student refund is calculated.

Medical leave may be approved retroactively when a documented condition prevented timely submission. A retroactive request must normally be filed within 30 calendar days after the student's last documented participation.

qa_pairs.question: My cumulative GPA is 3.30 and I want to register for 21 credits in Spring 2027 while keeping my Merit Scholarship. What is required, and what is the risk to the award?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring, so registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, which a 3.30 GPA satisfies, plus written approval from the programme director. The risk is renewal: the award requires at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, a term GPA of at least 3.30, and a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, so an overload that lowers the term GPA can trigger scholarship probation.

contexts.text: The normal undergraduate load is 12–18 credits in Fall or Spring and no more than 9 credits in Summer. Registration above 18 credits requires a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20 and written approval from the programme director.

To renew, a recipient must complete at least 12 graded Northstar credits in the reviewed term, earn a term GPA of at least 3.30, maintain a cumulative GPA of at least 3.20, and have no active serious-conduct sanction.
A first failure to meet one academic renewal requirement normally produces one term of scholarship probation rather than immediate loss. During probation, the award remains active.

qa_pairs.question: My instructor granted an `I` incomplete grade last term. What conditions had to be met, what happens if no grade is submitted by the deadline, and can this delay my graduation?
qa_pairs.expected_answer: An `I` incomplete may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently; the student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term, and if no grade is submitted by that deadline the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists. Graduation can be delayed, because a pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold, and the formal graduation application is due by the census date of the intended graduation term.

contexts.text: An `I` incomplete grade may be granted when at least 70% of assessed work is complete, the student was passing before an unexpected documented event, and the remaining work can be completed independently. The student and instructor must sign an incomplete plan. The default deadline is the end of the next regular term. If no grade is submitted by that deadline, the `I` converts to `F` unless an approved extension exists.
The formal graduation application is due by the census date of the intended graduation term. A late application may defer the conferral date even when all academic work is complete.
A pending grade appeal may delay conferral if the disputed course affects a degree requirement or GPA threshold.
